elements.element: Vendor defends third-party claims for Customer (and Affiliates)
elements.evidence: "Vendor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer and its Affiliates from and against any third-party claim"

elements.element: Indemnity covers allegations that Services/Deliverables infringe IP
elements.evidence: "(a) an allegation that the Services, Deliverables, or Vendor Technology infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right"

elements.element: Indemnity covers Vendor's breach of law
Indemnity covers data breach caused by Vendor
elements.evidence: "(c) any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor"

elements.element: Indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence/wilful misconduct
elements.evidence: "(d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct"
"shall give the indemnifying party prompt written notice of the claim"
"allow the indemnifying party to control the defence with counsel of its choice"
"provide reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying party's expense"

elements.element: Customer indemnity limited to Customer-provided content
elements.evidence: "arising out of content or materials provided by Customer for use in the Services (other than to the extent the claim is covered by Section 20.1)"

elements.element: Customer indemnity limited to Customer's breach of law
Fallback: Vendor IP indemnity with usual exclusions (modifications, combinations, specifications)
elements.evidence: "Customer's unauthorized modification ... combination with items not supplied or recommended by Vendor ... Vendor's compliance with written specifications supplied by Customer"

elements.element: Fallback: remedies procure, modify, replace, refund
elements.evidence: "procure the right for Customer to continue using them, or modify or replace them ... Vendor shall refund prepaid Fees"

elements.element: Fallback: Vendor indemnity subject to super-cap of 3x annual fees
elements.evidence: No super-cap language; 21.3 lists "its indemnification obligations" as Excluded Claims (uncapped), which is better for Customer

reasons: All atomic preferred elements are present in operative text: defend/indemnify for Customer and Affiliates, IP infringement, Vendor breach of law, Vendor-caused Customer Data breach, gross negligence/wilful misconduct, notice/control/cooperation procedure, and a Customer indemnity narrowed to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.

Fallback is incomplete (no 3x annual fees super-cap), but the levels are separate bargains and the locked preferred level is satisfied; the absence of a cap and the treatment of indemnification as an Excluded Claim in 21.3 favour Customer.

The article was entirely absent while 9.3 cross-references Section 20.5, so a concise standalone insertion is the minimum change; the infringement-remedy paragraph is necessary to cure the dangling 9.3 cross-reference, and the customary exclusions paragraph is confined to Section 20.1(a) and does not dilute the preferred indemnity heads.

No undefined terms introduced (Affiliate, Applicable Law, Customer Data, Deliverable, Vendor Technology, Fees, Order Form all defined); untouched Sections 9.3, 19.5 and 21.3 remain effective and now internally consistent.
